summary: Adversarial verification of companion claims C3, C4, C6, C8, C11, C12, C13, C14 (companion_claims.md). Verdict: every one of these eight claims is TRUE as stated; I found no counterexample, and each has a proof (sketched below) plus a numerical check (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thehonesttorus-github-io/9523ef6a-ff73-5ab2-8be3-275df2b5fcc6/scratchpad/wf/companion-verify/). Three minor imprecisions, none affecting truth: (i) C11's sup over b is unneeded (the flip bound uses b=0 only) and the closed-window convention with half-width 1 differs from Erdos's open-interval convention by up to a factor 2; (ii) C12's bound is loose by a factor 2 (commuting flips, continuous density at 0: ratio -> 1/2; non-commuting rotations are even less efficient, ratio ~1/4) and the resolvent certificate loses a further factor pi, so the bound is sharp (ratio 1) only when h sits between two separated spectral scales of A or h >= ||A||; (iii) C14's moving-algebra formula holds with delta_t = [U_t' U_t^*, .] (left generator); the right generator gives the same shape with a conjugated delta. The important finding is about RELEVANCE, not truth: C12/C11 are the robust (upper-bound, L2) version of the F6 kink-density mechanism and add nothing to the first-order law dm = eps*sigma*phi/2 for our commuting gates; C8's free/Dyson model has no odd free cumulants and so cannot represent the third-cumulant, realization-specific mean-zero memory of F1/F2 (its own 4th-moment caveat is the smaller gap); C14's Takesaki obstruction is vacuous in the commutative L^infty(Gaussian input) setting of our chain (conditional expectations onto every subalgebra exist), so F3's non-compressibility is not a modular obstruction; C13 is a true but unrelated caution; C3 and C4 are correct elementary facts with no quantitative link to F1-F7 beyond the 1/a amplification analogy for F4.

mechanisms.name: C3 alternating conditional expectations
mechanisms.statement: PROVED. In L^2(M,tau), E_P and E_Q are the orthogonal projections onto V_P=span{p_i}, V_Q=span{q_j}; J is the projection onto C1, and J <= E_P, E_Q with E_P J = J. Hence E_P E_Q - J = P'Q' with P' = E_P - J, Q' = E_Q - J orthogonal projections, and (E_P E_Q)^m - J = (P'Q')^m. In the orthonormal bases e_i = p_i/sqrt(pi_i), f_j = q_j/sqrt(theta_j) the compression of E_P E_Q is B_ij = tau(p_i q_j)/sqrt(pi_i theta_j) (real since tau(pq) = tau(qp) = conj tau(pq)), and J corresponds to the rank-one sqrt(pi) sqrt(theta)^T, so ||P'Q'|| = ||B - sqrt(pi)sqrt(theta)^T|| = ||C|| = rho. For the powers: (PQ)^m (QP)^m = (PQP)^{2m-1} (use QQ=Q, PP=P), so ||(PQ)^m||^2 = ||PQP||^{2m-1} = rho^{2(2m-1)}, i.e. ||(E_P E_Q)^m - J|| = rho^{2m-1}. Graph example: tau(p_u q_v) = A_uv/(nd), pi_u = theta_v = 1/n, so C = A/d - J_n and CC^T = A^2/d^2 - J_n (using A J_n = d J_n); rho = second largest |eigenvalue| of A/d.
mechanisms.where: companion_claims.md C3; proof above; check c3_check.py
mechanisms.status: PROVED + CHECKED (d=24, commuting and non-commuting partitions, exact to 1e-16; graph n=12, d=4)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Weak. The chain is not an alternating projection between two subalgebras; no quantity in F1-F7 is a product of conditional expectations. rho^{2m-1} is the classical maximal-correlation/principal-angle statement and says nothing about third-cumulant memory. At most an analogy to F7 (top singular vector of a centred cross-correlation = collective direction).

mechanisms.name: C4 rare conditioning identity
mechanisms.statement: PROVED. For b in N, phi_p(b) - tau(b) = tau((E_N(p) - a1) b)/a. Put x = E_N(p) - a1 in N, selfadjoint, tau(x) = 0. sup_{0<=b<=1, b in N} tau(xb) = tau(x_+) attained at b = 1_{(0,inf)}(x) in N; inf = -tau(x_-) = -tau(x_+); so sup |tau(xb)| = tau(x_+) = ||x||_1/2 (tau(x)=0 gives tau(x_+)=tau(x_-)). Hence sup = ||E_N(p) - a1||_1/(2a), attained. The remark that at a = e^{-cn} absolute errors n^{-100} are useless is the trivial consequence that an L1 error eps on E_N(p) becomes eps/(2a) on phi_p.
mechanisms.status: PROVED + CHECKED (d=24, N = M_8+M_8+M_8 block algebra, ranks 1,3,12: identity exact to 1e-8 and 2000 random b never exceed it)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Moderate as an analogy to F4/F6: conditioning on a small-probability set (kink density = small-ball density of the pre-activation at zero, F6) multiplies absolute errors by 1/a, the same mechanism as the capacity obstruction (3% residuals needed to 1e-2). But the identity is exact only for state restrictions of a conditional expectation onto a subalgebra; the chain's errors are not of that form, so it gives no new bound for us.

mechanisms.name: C6 log-volume drift
mechanisms.statement: PROVED. V(A) = -1/2 Tr log A has first derivative -1/2 Tr(A^{-1}H) and second derivative d^2/de^2 V(A+eH) = +1/2 Tr(A^{-1}HA^{-1}H). Ito for dA = sum_l H_l dB^l (independent BMs, H_l adapted selfadjoint, A_t invertible): dV = -1/2 Tr(A^{-1}dA) + 1/2 sum_l (1/2) Tr(A^{-1}H_l A^{-1}H_l) dt = -1/2 Tr(A^{-1}dA) + 1/4 Tr(A^{-1} eta(A^{-1})) dt with eta(b) = sum_l H_l b H_l. Pauli example A = diag(1,3): Tr(A^{-1}XA^{-1}X) = Tr(A^{-1}YA^{-1}Y) = 2/3, Tr(A^{-1}ZA^{-1}Z) = 1 + 1/9 = 10/9, while X^2 = Y^2 = Z^2 = I so eta(I) = I in all cases: eta(I) does not determine the drift.
mechanisms.status: PROVED + CHECKED (Pauli numbers exact; Hessian by finite differences matches 1/2 Tr(A^{-1}HA^{-1}H) to 1e-7; pathwise Euler-Maruyama martingale residual 1e-4 vs signal 0.09, shrinking with dt)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Structural analogy to F5: the Ito correction is a Laplacian of V along the noise directions, the same object as the Euler-Stein defect term (e - y.grad e - Lap e). The Pauli example parallels F2 (the needed quantity depends on the full covariance map eta, i.e. the bulk pairing, not on a current statistic like eta(I)). Analogy only; no theorem for the ReLU chain follows.

mechanisms.name: C8 free moment recursion and Dyson equation
mechanisms.statement: PROVED (standard operator-valued free probability). S = sum_l H_l (x) s_l with free standard semicirculars s_l is an M_d-valued semicircular with covariance E[S b S] = sum_l H_l b H_l = eta(b) (b in M_d (x) 1 commutes with 1 (x) s_l). B-valued moment-cumulant formula with only second cumulants for S and A_0 a constant in B: in E[X^r], X = A_0 + S, the first letter is A_0 (term A_0 M_{r-1}) or an S paired (non-crossingly) with the S at position j+2; the inside contributes E[X^j] = M_j nested in the cumulant, the outside M_{r-2-j}; so M_r = A_0 M_{r-1} + sum_{j=0}^{r-2} eta(M_j) M_{r-2-j}, M_0 = I, M_1 = A_0. Dyson: G_X(z) = G_S(z - A_0) = (z - A_0 - eta(G_X(z)))^{-1}. Cost: cache eta(M_j) once per j (m p d^3) and do the p^2/2 convolution products (p^2 d^3): O((mp+p^2)d^3) as stated.
mechanisms.status: PROVED + CHECKED (recursion vs GUE model d=3, m=2, N=600, 8 samples: relative error <= 5e-4 for r<=8, consistent with 1/N; Dyson vs empirical resolvent 2e-5; moment series -> Dyson solution to 8e-11 at z=12i, R=14)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Negative. The free model's moments are polynomials in A_0 and the second cumulant eta: it has no odd free cumulants. The quantity we need is the third-cumulant memory (F1), cubic in the last weight matrix and mean-zero over the weight ensemble (F2). A semicircular/Dyson substitute reproduces at most the Gaussian-closed leading order and removes exactly the object the chain computes; the companion's own caveat (Gaussian 4th moment 3 vs semicircular 2) is the smaller discrepancy.

mechanisms.name: C11 Littlewood-Offord gate flip bound
mechanisms.statement: PROVED (trivial). If z = S_v and |z - z~| <= h a.s., then 1_{z>0} != 1_{z~>0} forces z in (-h, h]: (z>0, z~<=0 gives z <= z~+h <= h; z<=0, z~>0 gives z >= z~-h > -h). So P(flip) <= P(|S_v| <= h) <= rho_h(v). Imprecision: the sup over b is not used (b = 0 suffices); and rho_h with closed windows of half-width 1 for v = ones is 2*binom(n,n/2)/2^n-ish (two lattice points), vs Erdos's open-interval bound binom(n,n/2)/2^n. The bound is attained by the adversarial perturbation z~ = z - h sgn(z).
mechanisms.status: PROVED + CHECKED (n=18, exact enumeration of 2^18 signs: adversarial flip = P(|S|<=h) <= rho_h at h=0.05..1; random perturbations ~1/4 of it; Gaussian small-ball 2h phi(0)/||v|| within 3%)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: It is the robust (upper bound) version of F6: for Gaussian pre-activations P(|z| <= h) = 2h phi(0)/sigma + O(h^3), which is the kink-density mechanism; F6's first-order law dm = eps sigma phi/2 is sharper (it gives the signed mean shift, not just the flipped mass). For the chain's classical gates nothing new follows.

mechanisms.name: C12 spectral gate stability (main inequality, identity, Holder and resolvent corollaries)
mechanisms.statement: PROVED. Write ||P-Q||_2^2 = tau(P(1-Q)) + tau((1-P)Q) (the cross terms vanish). Decompose P = sum_k P_k over eigenprojections of A with eigenvalue t_k > 0 (shells (t_k, t_{k+1}] with a refinement limit in a general finite vN algebra). Put X = (1-Q)P_k; since B commutes with 1-Q and A P_k = t_k P_k: (B - t_k) X = (1-Q)(B - A)P_k = (1-Q)E P_k, and B - t_k <= -t_k on Ran(1-Q), so ||X||_2 <= ||(1-Q)EP_k||_2/t_k <= h sqrt(tau P_k)/t_k (this is the Davis-Kahan sin-theta theorem, Bhatia VII.3.1, with a one-point spectrum). With the trivial bound tau(P_k(1-Q)P_k) <= tau(P_k): tau(P(1-Q)) = sum_k tau(P_k(1-Q)P_k) <= sum_k tau(P_k) min(1, h^2/t_k^2) = tau(P min(1,h^2/A^2)). Same for (1-P)Q with eigenvalues t_k <= 0 (eigenvalue 0 gets weight 1). Sum: ||P-Q||_2^2 <= tau(min(1,h^2/A^2)). Identity: min(1,h^2/t^2) = int_h^inf 1_{|t|<=s} 2h^2/s^3 ds, so tau(min) = 2h^2 int_h^inf Q_A(s)/s^3 ds. Holder: Q_A <= Ct^a + delta gives 2C h^a/(2-a) + delta. Resolvent: -h Im tau((ih-A)^{-1}) = tau(h^2/(h^2+A^2)) and min(1,h^2/t^2) <= 2h^2/(h^2+t^2), so <= 2R_A(h). Sharpness: commuting flip E = -h sgn(A) gives LHS = Q_A(h); with a continuous density rho(0) at 0, LHS ~ 2 rho(0) h while the bound ~ 4 rho(0) h (ratio 1/2) and 2R_A(h) ~ 2 pi rho(0) h (ratio 1/pi); non-commuting rotations of a pair (t, -t') give LHS/bound ~ 2(tt')^2/((t+t')^2(t^2+t'^2)) <= 1/4; ratio -> 1 iff A's spectrum splits into a part inside [-h,h] and a part far outside (bimodal), including h >= ||A||.
mechanisms.status: PROVED + CHECKED (d=60 GUE, 13 values of h in [1e-3, 4]: random E, commuting flip, unitary +-h, hill-climb from the flip, and 400 random (A,E) pairs: max LHS/bound = 0.98, never > 1; commuting flip ratio 0.41-0.72 for h in [0.02,1], -> 1.00 at h = 2 = ||A||; semicircle continuum limit 0.504 at h=0.02; bimodal spectrum ratio = 1.000 for h between the two scales; LHS/2R_A at most 0.73, 1/pi-ish at small h)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: This is F6 in matrix form. In the chain the gates D(Phi) are diagonal (commuting case), where the exact flipped mass is Q_A(h) and the bound costs a factor 2; pre-activations have a continuous density at 0 so we are in the ratio-1/2 regime, not the tight bimodal regime. It gives an L2 size of the flipped gates, not the signed mean shift that drives the MSE (F6: dm = eps sigma phi/2; 1e-3 variance error -> 7x MSE). No route around F3/F4 follows from it.

mechanisms.name: C13 Clifford obstruction
mechanisms.statement: PROVED. S^2 = (1/m)[sum_i Gamma_i^2 + sum_{i<j} eps_i eps_j (Gamma_i Gamma_j + Gamma_j Gamma_i)] = (1/m) m I = I for every sign choice; S traceless, so its spectral law is (delta_{-1} + delta_1)/2 with atoms of mass 1/2 independent of m, versus the classical Rademacher atom ~ sqrt(2/(pi m)). Hence no anti-concentration bound in terms of the operator norms ||Gamma_i|| = 1 alone.
mechanisms.status: PROVED + CHECKED (Jordan-Wigner m=6 in dimension 8: all 64 sign patterns give ||S^2 - I|| <= 6e-16, eigenvalues +-1 with multiplicity 4)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: None for the classical problem: the gates are scalar thresholds on Gaussian pre-activations; F4's zero-mean-sketch obstruction is an odd-moment/parity fact, not an anti-concentration failure. Valid only as a caution against transplanting Littlewood-Offord into an operator-valued reformulation.

mechanisms.name: C14 modular group, cocycle, Takesaki criterion, qubit obstruction, moving algebras
mechanisms.statement: PROVED. For phi = tau(rho .) on a tracial algebra, Delta = L_rho R_rho^{-1} so sigma_s(a) = rho^{is} a rho^{-is}; Gibbs rho = e^{-beta H}/Z gives sigma_s = alpha_{-beta s}. u_s(t) = D_t^{is} D_0^{-is} is unitary and D_t^{is} a D_t^{-is} = u_s (D_0^{is} a D_0^{-is}) u_s^*. Takesaki (1972): a phi-preserving normal conditional expectation onto N exists iff sigma^phi_s(N) = N for all s. Qubit: rho = diag(p,q), p = (1+r)/2: sigma_s(X) = cos(theta)X - sin(theta)Y with theta = s log(p/q), not in span{I,X} when r != 0. Elementary confirmation: a phi-preserving N-bimodular E must satisfy phi(e_+ a e_-) = phi(E(e_+ a e_-)) = 0 for all a, i.e. e_- rho e_+ = 0, i.e. [rho, X] = 0, false for rho = (I+rZ)/2, r != 0. Moving algebras: with U_t' = K_t U_t, K anti-Hermitian, delta_t = [K_t, .]: d/dt Ad(U_t) = delta_t Ad(U_t), d/dt Ad(U_t)^{-1} = -Ad(U_t)^{-1} delta_t, so dE_t/dt = delta_t E_t - E_t delta_t. Imprecision: with the right generator U_t' = U_t K_t the same formula holds with delta replaced by [U_t K_t U_t^*, .]; the note does not say which.
mechanisms.status: PROVED + CHECKED (qubit r=0.6: sigma_s(X) formula exact, distance from span{I,X} = 0.57 at s=0.3; linear feasibility of a phi-preserving bimodular E: residual 0.30 for rho=(I+rZ)/2 (infeasible), 1e-16 for rho=(I+rX)/2 and rho=I/2 (feasible); cocycle identity 4e-15 in M_3; moving-algebra derivative residual 1e-9 vs scale 3.6)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: None in the chain's actual setting: the algebra is commutative (functions of the Gaussian input), the modular group of any state is trivial, and state-preserving conditional expectations onto every subalgebra exist. Therefore the non-compressibility and Hadamard obstruction (F1, F3) are not Takesaki-type obstructions, and 'moving algebras' is a tautology about conjugated projections. It could only matter if the problem were recast with a genuinely non-tracial noncommutative state, which the companion does not do.

caveats: Only the eight requested claims were examined (C1, C2, C5, C7, C9, C10 not checked). All numerics are finite-dimensional (M_d with normalized trace); the proofs of C3, C4, C13, C14 are fully general for finite partitions / finite vN algebras, C6 needs A_t to stay invertible (the first SDE run left the positive cone and had to be restarted deeper inside it), C8 relies on standard operator-valued free probability (B-valued semicircular moment-cumulant formula) and the GUE comparison is at N=600 with 8 samples (relative accuracy 5e-4), and the C12 proof is written for matrices with the general-algebra case by spectral shells plus the Davis-Kahan sin-theta theorem (Bhatia VII.3.1) and a refinement limit that I sketched but did not write out. The C12 'hill-climb' adversary is a local random search, not a global optimum; the analytic argument (pair rotation ratio <= 1/4 < commuting flip ratio 1/2) is what rules out non-commuting violations at small h, and the general proof rules them out everywhere. Relevance judgments to F1-F7 are mine, based on the problem file and REPORT.md lines 12-28 and 99; I did not rerun any chain code.
